newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-LOLA TO BEAT STEWART, SAYS TEAM CHIEF.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LOLA TO BEAT STEWART, SAYS TEAM CHIEF.

text.p: Lola team chief Eric Broadley forecast on Tuesday his unfancied team would beat fellow-debutants Stewart and make a competitive first impression on Formula One this year.

Broadley, founder and principal of Lola who are making their first entry in Grand Prix racing as a team in their own right following their success as car builders in other racing including the Indycar series in the United States, said he would be disappointed if his team failed to outrace Stewart.

"We can beat them and we certainly should beat them," he said at Lola's base at Huntingdon in central England. "If we don't beat them, then we deserve to be given a good kick up the backside. With our experience and back-up, it should be no problem."

Broadley said also that Lola, powered by a 1994-vintage Ford V8 engine for the first part of the season, will hope to outpace world champion Damon Hill's Arrows Yamaha car as well as the Stewarts, powered by factory-backed Ford V10's.
"They will certainly be a benchmark for us," he said.

Lola has raced in Formula One several times before as a supplier of chassis, but never as an entrant in its own right. The team plan to introduce their own V10 engines to power their car in the second half of the season.
Lola has a budget of 35 million dollars for the year, said Broadley. This compares reasonably with the 50 million dollars budget of the Benetton team.

"It is exciting for us to be involved in Formula One, but we are not going into it with over-optimistic expectations," said Broadley. "If we get any podium finishes this year, I think it will be down to luck."
Italian Vincenzo Sospiri and Brazilian Ricardo Rosset are the team drivers but the Lola car is not expected to be launched for at least another three weeks.
The Formula One world championship starts in Melbourne with the Australian Grand Prix on March 9.
